entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-11-12
entry.content:
The sub spent this run on the stock rising in the morning and fading by the close, on whether Nvidia's trouble helps Google, and on a rumoured model codenamed Krypton. The real change came from Google: on 10 November, Gemini 4 Carbon opened to paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers. Google had announced it on 28 October, and the 30 October and 6 November runs missed that. Google also put Gemini for healthcare into preview, released a Gemini Decisions API, and opened pre-orders for Gemini eyewear.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-11-09
entry.content:
A thin run. Most of the hot list is still the threads covered on 6 November, and the new posts are price calls, a Jim Cramer screenshot and a question about an unnamed "Nvidia scandal". The real news came from Google, not the sub. Google announced two more eighth-generation TPU systems today, and on 5 November it committed $17 billion to its first Wyoming data centre, then took over the site from Crusoe. Strictly, nothing passes this feed's two-test Must know bar. The TPU launch is confirmed by Google and changes what Alphabet sells, but the sub had not reached it when this ran. It leads below because the format requires one item, and its Status line says so.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-11-06
entry.content:
This run covers the week after Q3 results and the 3 November midterms. The sub spent it watching GOOG hold roughly flat while chip and neocloud stocks fell on Thursday 5 November, and most of it reads a slower data-centre build-out as good for Alphabet. Company news was thin: Alphabet closed a €6 billion euro bond on 5 November, Reuters reported Google's voluntary buyouts have spread to five more countries, and a K-12 Search change drew a small, angry thread. The gap since the last entry is seven days, so official sources were checked for the whole window.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-30
entry.content:
Every hot post this run is about the Q3 results Alphabet reported on 28 October and the sell-off that followed. Posters put the fall at 12.6% to 14%. The sub mostly answers it with "don't panic sell" and buying the dip. The arguments that engage with the numbers are about three things: negative free cash flow, Search slowing to 12% growth, and the CFO's line that capital spending will "increase significantly" in 2027. The release and the 10-Q confirm the headline figures. The quoted share-price moves were not checked.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-27
entry.content:
The day before results, the sub's largest thread marks the stock turning negative for the year, and nearly every top reply is a long-term holder saying the price does not matter or that they bought more. The arguments that do engage with the business are about capital spending: whether a high capex figure on 28 October means another drop, and whether Google's rented compute and Cloud backlog justify it. The one company story the sub discussed, Finland's order halting site clearance at two Google data-centre projects, dates from 6 October. Nothing passed the Must know test: results land tomorrow, not in this window, and the confirmed announcements since the last entry drew no discussion.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-24
entry.content:
Four days before results, the sub is in drawdown mode: threads call it a bear market, ask why the stock "keeps bleeding" and whether to buy before or after the print, and the best-received replies are long-term holders saying the price is a sale. The one thing that changed in the window is a deal: OpenAI's models are coming to Google Cloud, announced by both companies on 21 October. Reaction in the sub was split between reading it as another way for Google to earn and as a retreat from the frontier race.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-21
entry.content:
One week before results, the sub has stopped arguing about Argon and started counting down. The two newest threads are about the stock losing its 200-day moving average and whether it will see $360 again, and in both the best-received answers are that only the 28 October print matters now. The run's top post by score is a Motley Fool prediction of triple-digit Google Cloud growth that the sub's own top comments dismiss as a source. Nothing passed the Must know test: no earnings, guidance or filing has landed yet, the one confirmed launch in the window drew no discussion at all, and the sub's dominant attention is on a date rather than on an event.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-17
entry.content:
The sub's complaint about Argon has flipped from "where is it" to "is this it". Three days after the launch the loudest threads are about whether the reception matters for the stock at all, and the best-received answers say it doesn't — macro and the capital spending update do. Meanwhile two Google announcements inside this window got almost no discussion: Universal Cart launched in the US, and Google Quantum AI published a Willow error-correction result in Science. No story passed the Must know test this run: the one confirmed launch that changes what Alphabet sells drew four comments rather than dominant attention, and there was no filing, guidance or regulatory event.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-14
entry.content:
The wait the last two entries described is over: Google made Gemini 4 Argon globally available on 13 October, two weeks after announcing it. The sub's reaction is not relief but puzzlement that the stock barely moved, and the complaint thread posted the day before — that Meta teased and shipped a frontier model in one day while Argon sat unreleased — now reads as the high-water mark of the frustration. Everything else on the hot list is material the last two entries already covered.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-11
entry.content:
A thin run, three days after a dense one. Most of the hot list is the same material the last entry covered — Gemini 4 Argon, the Constellation nuclear deals, Gemini agent, the free-tier limits — plus the usual position posts, which this feed skips. The one genuinely new story is a Business Insider report, picked up by the sub, that Google is internally testing a Gemini 4 build codenamed Carbon. No story passed the Must know test this run: nothing was confirmed by Google, no filing or guidance landed, and there was no regulatory event.

entry.title: GOOG stock digest, 2026-10-08
entry.content:
The sub is preoccupied with Gemini 4 Argon. Google announced it on 30 September, but most people still can't use it, and the stock fell on the news. Members read that as the market pricing in slow execution. Real announcements got a muted reception: a 20-year nuclear power deal with Constellation, and a "universal" Gemini agent for enterprises.
